observation.visible_scene: An aerial/drone view of a steep alpine ridge: dark green grassy slopes with scattered white snow patches on the upper ridgelines, a deep saddle (gully) running diagonally through the center, and a large bank of white fog/cloud occupying the right side of the frame. A rounded green foreground shoulder sits at center-right, with a small patch of vegetation/tree on its right slope. The terrain itself is static; the only moving elements are the fog and the camera viewpoint.
visible_changes: The fog stream inside the central gully continuously morphs and drifts, its bright white plume shifting shape and position from frame to frame (e.g., the dense tongue at the gully mouth moves and re-forms between t=0.0s and t=2.67s).

The fog wrapping the right shoulder of the foreground ridge changes form: in early frames a soft tongue covers the slope near (650,700), while by the last frames the fog has redistributed and a small tree/vegetation patch on that right slope becomes more exposed and clearly visible near (760,740).
The right-edge fog bank and the upper-right sky/fog boundary slowly change shape and density across the segment, indicating ongoing cloud movement rather than a fixed backdrop.

The camera drifts slowly: comparing first and last frames, the background peak moves from about (360,110) to (360,130) and the foreground shoulder apex from about (530,520) to (540,580), i.e. a slight downward/rightward shift of the whole scene, consistent with a slow pan/tilt (or small forward move) rather than any object translating.

The isolated snow patch at the bottom center, visible in the first frames (~600,950), shifts toward and partly out of the bottom edge as the viewpoint changes, while a small snow fleck near the bottom reappears around (500,990) late in the clip.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the fog is overall building, holding, or dissipating beyond this window, and its source or direction of origin.
The cause of the camera drift (operator input vs. wind buffeting) and any motion before t=0 or after t=2.67s.
Whether the exposed tree/vegetation was previously occluded by fog or simply outside the earlier framing.
uncertain_details: Exact camera motion vector (pan vs. tilt vs. dolly) is ambiguous because the parallax between foreground and background is small.
Distinguishing fog advancing over the ridge from fog merely receding/re-shaping is uncertain; the right-side change could be either.
Frame-to-frame fog differences are partly due to viewpoint shift, so the true flow speed of the cloud cannot be isolated from the camera drift.
